message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to spin‑up a **Compute Engine** VM that has a high‑end NVIDIA GPU (the closest match to an “RTX A6000” that’s actually sold by Google Cloud – *nvidia‑tesla‑a100*) running **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important:**  
> • Google Cloud does **not** offer an exact “RTX A6000” SKU.  
> • The nearest equivalent is `nvidia-tesla-a100` (Ampere).  
> • You can replace the accelerator type with another supported GPU (`p100`, `v100`, `k80`, …) if needed.  

---

## 1️⃣ Quick start via `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables -------------------------------------------------------------
PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE   ="us-central1-b"          # pick your preferred zone
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Create the instance -----------------------------------------------
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-highmem-16" \            # 16 vCPU / 104 GB RAM
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1" \
    --guest-os-features="GPU_TESLA_A100" \
    --preemptible=false \
    --no-restart-on-failure \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="canonical-cloud" \
    --disk-size=500GB \
    --network-interface="subnet=$ZONE-subnet,access-configs=[{}]" \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --metadata-from-file=startup-script=/dev/null     # no custom script yet
```

### What each option means

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU + memory allocation. Adjust per workload. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU. Change `count=` if you need more. |
| `--guest-os-features` | Enables GPU driver support inside the OS. |
| `--image-family & --image-project` | Boots from Canonical's official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--disk-size` | Size of the persistent boot disk. Increase if you plan heavy workloads. |

After creation, install the NVIDIA drivers manually (or add them to a startup script):

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
wget https://dl.nvidia.com/nvidia-docker/gpgkey
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | sudo apt-key add -
apt-get update
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
```

(Or pull a pre‑built Docker container that already contains CUDA.)

---

## 2️⃣ Full REST API payload

If you prefer to hit the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the minimal JSON body you’d post to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/instances
```

Replace `<PROJECT>` and `<ZONE>` with your values.

```json
{
  "name": "<INSTANCE_NAME>",
  "machineType": "projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-highmem-16",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/canonical-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 500
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network":"global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs":[{"kind":"compute#accessConfig","name":"External NAT"}]
    }
  ],
  "labels": {"purpose":"demo"},
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "reservationAffinity":{
    "consumeReservationType":"ANY_RESERVATION"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": []
  }
}
```

#### How to execute

Using `curl` (you’ll need OAuth 2.0 bearer token):

```bash
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances"
```

Where `instance.json` holds the above JSON.

---

## 3️⃣ Optional: Terraform template

For reproducibility, here’s a tiny Terraform module you can drop into your repo:

```hcl
provider "google" {
  project = var.project_id
  region  = var.region
}

resource "google_compute_instance" "rtxa6000_demo" {
  name         = "rtx-a6000-demo"
  machine_type = "n1-highmem-16"
  zone         = "${var.region}-b"

  boot_disk {
    initialize_params {
      image = "canonical-cloud/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      size_gb = 500
    }
  }

  network_interface {
    network       = "default"
    access_config {}
  }

  service_account {
    scopes = ["cloud-platform"]
  }

  guest_accelerator {
    type  = "nvidia-tesla-a100"
    count = 1
  }

  metadata_startup_script = <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
EOF
}
```

Run:

```bash
terraform init
terraform apply
```

--- 

### Recap

* **Google Cloud doesn’t ship an RTX A6000**, so we’re provisioning a `nvidia-tesla-a100`.  
* Pick a suitable machine type (here `n1-highmem-16`).  
* Boot from Canonical’s Ubuntu 20.04 LTS family image.  
* Add the GPU via either `gcloud`, REST, or Terraform.  

Happy hacking! 🚀
